subject: Request: temporary credit reinstatement for Arboretum Health trial
messages:
From: Lindsey Hart <lindsey.hart@arborethealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@arborethealth.com>
Date: Sat, 2 Oct 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Trial environment access and credits after pilot expiration

Hi Ben,

We shipped our integration tests last week and started ramping internal demos, but the trial account hit the credit cap yesterday and the sandbox shut down. Procurement is still finalizing PO language (they're asking for a short SOW and SOC2 evidence). Our engineering and product stakeholders are blocked on demoing to the exec team next week.

Can Redwood make a one-time credit reinstatement or temporary extension while procurement completes? We don't need an open-ended arrangement — just enough to run demos and a short pilot (est. 60–90 days). If there are any approval forms we need to sign or a conditional authorization, tell me and I'll run it through legal.

Really appreciate any flexibility — we like the perf and cost profile so far.

Thanks,
Lindsey Hart
Director of Product
Arboretum Health

P.S. attaching a list of the test flows that are blocked (not included here).

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lindsey Hart <lindsey.hart@arborethealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Trial environment access and credits after pilot expiration

Lindsey —

Thanks for the note and sorry to hear you hit the cap at a bad time. We can absolutely help keep the trial moving while procurement completes. Quick summary of options so Procurement/Legal can pick a path:

- Option A: One-time credit reinstatement (non-renewing) — 90 days of sandbox credits tied to account RDW-4872. Requires signed authorization from an authorized Arboretum rep.
- Option B: Conditional short-term extension — 60 days, auto-expire, no financial commitment, we can restrict model/throughput to control cost.
- Option C: Temporary developer seats + lower-tier reserved throughput for demo windows (costed, requires billing contact).

If you want Option A or B I can route for a one-off approval. I am cc'ing Marissa (Account Lead) to confirm the internal approval path and Jordan (Sales Ops) for the authorization doc and finance sign-off.

Tell me which option Procurement prefers and we'll move fast.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0192

--
Attachment: none in this message

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 5 Oct 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Trial environment access and credits after pilot expiration

Ben/Jordan —

For Arboretum (RDW-4872) I'm comfortable approving a one-time 90-day credit reinstatement capped at $6,000 usage equivalent provided we get:
1) Signed one-time credit authorization from Arboretum legal (name + title + date)
2) Confirmation of procurement PO timeline (procurement@arborethealth.com)
3) Scope limits: limit to inference endpoints A and B; disable burst over 4 rps unless Ben requests temporary lift during exec demos.

Jordan — please prepare the authorization PDF and route to finance for the internal ledger entry. Once we have the signed doc back from Arboretum we'll push the credits live and send Lindsey the service window and usage tracking.

Marissa
Sr. Manager, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
